lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Date of birth and nationality are personal details conventionally left off a résumé.
items.because: They are not relevant to assessing qualifications and can distract from information a reader should weigh.

items.says: Education appears before experience despite more than four years of work before the MBA.
items.because: It makes education seem like the main emphasis and gives less attention to the work history.

items.says: The checkout-conversion increase is attributed to the flow change without a stated comparison or measurement basis.
items.because: Other factors during the measurement period could explain the increase.

items.says: The 35% conversion increase does not say whether it is relative or in percentage points, or identify the comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the figure represents or judge its scale.

items.says: “For all merchants” adds no clarification to the conversion result.
items.because: It does not explain the 35% figure or its basis.

items.says: The dispute self-service bullet gives a delivery-timing result but no post-launch outcome.
items.because: It does not show whether the feature improved the dispute experience or reduced support work.

items.says: The delivery result appears after the requirements and stakeholder list.
items.because: That makes the result easier to miss on a scan.

items.says: The annual chargeback-loss estimate lacks an annualization basis and a definition of loss.
items.because: Six months of data do not by themselves show how the $1.1 million figure was calculated.

items.says: The estimate and its roadmap consequence appear after a long list of methods.
items.because: A reader has to get through the methods before reaching the result and why it mattered.

items.says: The phrase explaining the roadmap impact is bulky.
items.because: It takes several words to explain a straightforward consequence of the estimate.

items.says: “Over the summer” repeats the time period shown in the entry dates.
items.because: Repeating the period adds no useful information.

items.says: The comparison bullet reports no result from comparing merchants in the new and old flows.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what changed or whether the new flow performed better.

items.says: The Harbor Payments bullets cover several efforts without building one clear story.
items.because: A reader moving between checkout, disputes, chargebacks, triage and onboarding may not see a clear thread through the internship.

items.says: The bullet credits a reduction in late deliveries to excluding weather-delayed shipments from the calculation.
items.because: The exclusion can improve the reported rate without making any delivery less late.

items.says: The quarterly review and forecast-pack responsibilities have no stated business outcome.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the recurring work enabled or changed.

items.says: The bullet uses present tense for a role that ended in August 2023.
items.because: It makes a completed responsibility sound ongoing.

items.says: The 1,800-hour saving is not tied to a comparison baseline.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the saving was measured against.

items.says: The annual hours saved appear after the rollout and training details.
items.because: That makes the result easy to miss on a scan.

items.says: The amount redistributed does not establish that the food would otherwise have been thrown away.
items.because: Pickup records show how much was redistributed, not what would have happened without the app.

items.says: The bullet links the shift system to the slot-fill rate and fewer staff cover shifts without establishing causation.
items.because: The outcomes could also reflect changes in demand, scheduling or staffing.

items.says: The weekly sessions describe activity but not what the scheduling work changed.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the sessions improved access, reduced delays or led to another useful change.

items.says: The bullet does not show how much the intake form was shortened or what practical effect the change had.
items.because: Adoption does not show whether the revision made intake faster or easier.

items.says: Passive wording obscures the candidate’s role in mapping intake and shortening the form.
items.because: A reader may not be able to tell what the candidate personally contributed.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding result is duplicated under the internship and the hospital practicum.
items.because: It credits the result to two different entries, although the practicum is for a hospital network.
